cross_mode_rule.statement: Two simultaneous spatial orders a, b (both injectable, m does not divide a, b; c = 1) give module power pulsation at f_a + f_b iff m | (a+b) and at |f_a - f_b| iff m | (a-b), amplitude m V_a I_b (+ m V_b I_a). For m = 3 one of the two always holds (a, b in {1, 2} mod 3) -> every overlap / injection pulsates every cell. For prime m >= 5 choose a != +-b (mod m) -> no pulsation.

open_end_two_modules.average_imbalance: share alpha of the coil voltage set by modulation: P_A = alpha P, P_B = (1 - alpha) P; alpha = 0.5 balanced, and alpha is itself a balancing knob (full +-100 % of the pair power)
open_end_two_modules.isolated_neutral: a module whose 3 legs all feed open-end coils to one partner module keeps zero current sum -> admissible
open_end_two_modules.hardware: switching between star (2p8) and open-end (2p4) connection needs contactors/extra legs - outside H10
open_end_two_modules.pulsation: none if both modules carry the same balanced set

dc_voltage_reallocation.condition: admissible iff P_j / V_j is equal for all cells (same I_dc); a 1 % mismatch drifts as in drift_per_1pct_imbalance
dc_voltage_reallocation.note: per-mode reallocation must move module power in exact proportion to the new cell voltages, through the balancing knobs below

cell_to_coil_reassignment.note: reassigning coils to modules electronically is not possible without switches; any reassignment that leaves modules with unequal coil counts gives average imbalance = (coil-count spread)/(mean)

zero_sequence_circulation.why: isolated neutrals: no current path between modules

per_module_common_mode_voltage.why: CM voltage drives no current in an isolated-neutral module; it only moves the neutral potential

same_frequency_balancing_order.principle: inject a current of order b with m | (p - b)/c (and m not dividing b) at f_e: the difference term is DC, dP_j = m V I_b cos(phi_j), phi_j varies with the module position -> zero-sum redistribution; orders b = p +- m, p +- 2m, ... give all spatial harmonics over the N modules (complete basis for zero-mean imbalance vectors)
same_frequency_balancing_order.m5_note: for m = 5 the balancing orders (b = 9, 14, 19 for p = 4) are high and have low winding factors -> weaker knob per ampere; the same property that removes cross-mode pulsation removes the low-order balancing knobs
same_frequency_balancing_order.limits: needs back-EMF (speed > 0): at standstill the knob is only I R; the b-order field induces rotor currents in an IM (extra loss, small torque ripple)

module_current_scaling.principle: scale module j currents by (1 + e_j), sum e_j = 0: dP_j = e_j P_j; equivalent to a set of b-orders; distorts MMF by |e|

dc_side.note: cell-to-cell DC-DC balancers or a bypass would be extra hardware (not zero-hardware)

balancing_headroom.verdict: DC (average) imbalances are cheap to correct: 1 % costs about 1 A of balancing current at cruise. AC pulsations at f_a + f_b are not removable by these knobs within the module current budget at the 100s-of-W/A scale and must be avoided (mode/order choice, m >= 5) or absorbed by capacitance.

admissible_mode_set.steady_modes: admissible iff T08 rule (i) equal leg magnitude, (ii) module unit-sum zero, (iii) module square-sum zero; 5079 of 5232 enumerated modes pass; (iii)-violators need C_required (see examples) or are excluded. Prefer interleaved module partitions (eccentricity cancels).

IM_handover_m3.rule: overlapped 8->4 handover pulsates each cell at f8 + f4; admissible only as a sequential handover with cross product below max_overlap_product_for_5pct, i.e. essentially no overlap -> torque gap (simulator: ~0.13 s at t_d = 0.01 s)

admissible_mode_set.IM_handover_m5plus: admissible with full overlap (torque-gap-free) when m does not divide (p1 +- p2)/c
admissible_mode_set.H09_open_end: admissible (alpha = 0.5), alpha doubles as a balancing knob; star/open-end switching is hardware
admissible_mode_set.H05_series_parking: inadmissible without DC bypass hardware: a parked cell (P_j = 0) still carries I_dc and charges at I_dc/C (e.g. I_dc = 250 A -> 248016 V/s)
admissible_mode_set.IM_handover_m3_corrected: crossfade (factor 1.39 in the model): C_req 15.6 mF at +-10 %, 31.3 mF at +-5 % (flat). See screen_H11.json for the pulsation-constrained schedule.

summary_text: H10 screen. Average (DC) imbalance is zero for every mode that passes the T08 winding rule and is cheap to trim with same-frequency balancing orders (about 1 A per 1 % at cruise). The binding constraint is AC power pulsation: in a 3-leg isolated-neutral module any two simultaneous spatial orders a, b give pulsation at f_a + f_b or |f_a - f_b| with amplitude 3 V I. This hits (1) the overlapped IM 8/4 handover (8.5 kW per cell at 210 Hz, 2.5x the cell mean, C needed 22.8 mF vs 1.0-2.9 mF available), (2) the WRSM k-sweep, (3) H03 harmonic excitation, (4) steady WRSM space harmonics. For prime m >= 5 the pulsation vanishes when a != +-b (mod m), so m = 5/7 makes overlapped (torque-gap-free) transitions and harmonic excitation admissible, at the cost of weaker low-order balancing knobs. Series-cell parking (H05) is inadmissible without bypass hardware. Admissible set: steady modes with rule (i)-(iii); m = 3 transitions sequential (torque gap) or with sized capacitance; m >= 5 overlapped transitions with m not dividing (p1 +- p2)/c.

sanity_time_domain.expected: m3 (4,2): 3; m5/m7 (4,2): 0; m3 (4,8): 3; m5 (4,8): 0; m6 (4,2): 6; one mode (4,4) m3 at one frequency: 0 pulsation, mean 3 cos; one mode p=3 in m6: pulsation 6 (fails rule iii)

crossfade_model.note: naive linear 0.25 s CURRENT crossfade (no flux forcing) in the two-mode RFOC model: the terminal voltage follows the rotor flux, which lags the current by tau_r (0.48 s for 2p8, 1.46 s for 2p4), so V8 stays high while I4 rises and the envelope factor exceeds 1. The ideal x(1-x) = 0.25 assumes the fluxes track the currents instantly. The true factor of a flux-forced overlapped schedule lies between; the simulator's MEC run (confirm_H10) decides.

sequential_V8_I4_term.note: 'sequential' = drop all 2p8 current, then build 2p4 under the pulsation limit; the decaying 2p8 rotor flux still induces V8, so 3 V8 I4 limits the 2p4 build current until the flux has decayed

balancing_knob_correction.statement: The power shift per ampere of a same-frequency balancing order b is m V_p (main-mode leg voltage x m), independent of the winding factor of b. Signed orders count: for p = 4, m = 5 the order b = -1 (counter-rotating 2-pole) satisfies 5 | (p - b). So m = 5 is NOT a weaker knob (H10 said so - corrected).
